```{r libraries, message = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(PKNCA)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250211)
set.seed(20250211)
```

Ndzamba et al. (2025) modelled ethambutol pharmacokinetics in 61 South African
adults with newly diagnosed drug-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis and HIV
from the TB-HAART study, and used the model to evaluate the WHO weight-band
doses for the 275 mg first-line fixed-dose combination and the 400 mg tablet
used in MDR-TB regimens.

```{r load_model}
mod <- nlmixr2lib::readModelDb("Ndzamba_2025_ethambutol")
```

Reference: Ndzamba B, Denti P, McIlleron H, Smith P, Mthiyane T, Rustomjee R,
Onyebujoh P, Resendiz-Galvan JE, Wasserman S (2025). Pharmacokinetics of
ethambutol and weight banded dosing in South African adults newly diagnosed
with tuberculosis and HIV. *Antimicrob Agents Chemother* 69(2):e01200-24.
[doi:10.1128/aac.01200-24](https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.01200-24)

## Population

| Characteristic | Overall (N = 61) |
|---|---|
| Age (years) | 32.0 [27-37] |
| Female | 33 (54.1%) |
| Weight (kg) | 55.2 [50.0-62.4] |
| Height (m) | 1.59 [1.54-1.68] |
| Fat-free mass (kg) | 42 [36.3-45.5] |
| CD4+ T-cell count (cells/uL) | 254 [159-323] |
| Creatinine clearance (mL/min) | 97 [80.1-117] |
| e-275 Rifafour formulation | 54 (88.5%) |
| Started ART on day 13 | 41 (67.2%) |

Values are median [IQR] or n (%), reproducing Table 1 of the source. All
participants were HIV-positive and ART-naive at enrolment. Ethambutol was given
once daily after an overnight fast in a four-drug fixed-dose combination with
275 mg ethambutol hydrochloride per tablet, by weight band: 550 mg below
37.9 kg (1 participant), 825 mg for 38-54.9 kg (31), 1100 mg for 55-70 kg (19)
and 1375 mg above 70 kg (10). PK visits were on days 0, 7, 14 and 28, with
samples at 1, 1.5, 2, 4, 8 and 12 h after the observed dose and pre-dose samples
on days 7, 14 and 28 (plus one on day 13).

**Doses in the model are mg of ethambutol base**: the authors converted the
hydrochloride dose with the salt factor 0.737 (MW 204.31 / 277.23), so each
275 mg tablet is 202.68 mg of base. Convert a hydrochloride dose the same way
before simulation. Doses go into `transit1`, the first of the four transit
compartments, not into `depot`.

## Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source location; this
table is the vignette-level summary.

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure | 2-compartment; 4 transit compartments (NN = 3) into an absorption compartment | Results; Figure S2; supplementary control stream `$MODEL` (ADVAN5, 7 compartments) |
| CL/F, Vc/F (FFM 42 kg) | 34.8 L/h, 156 L | Table 2 + footnote c; control stream `TVFFM = 42` |
| Q/F, Vp/F (WT 57 kg) | 34.4 L/h, 564 L | Table 2 + footnote d; control stream `TVWT = 57` |
| ka, MTT, NN | 0.877 1/h, 0.717 h, 3 fixed | Table 2; control stream `KTR = (NN+1)/MTT` |
| F | 1 fixed | Table 2 |
| Allometry | FFM on CL and Vc, total weight on Q and Vp; exponents 0.75 / 1 fixed | Methods; Results; control stream `ALLMCL_FFM`, `ALLMV_FFM`, `ALLMCL_WT`, `ALLMV_WT` |
| FFM equation | Janmahasatian, sex-specific constants, height in m | Control stream `$PK` |
| Antib-4 effect | F x 1.260, MTT x 1.371 | Table 2; control stream `THETA(14)`, `THETA(15)` |
| BSV CL | 19.9% | Table 2 |
| BOV ka / F / MTT | 52.8% / 27.8% / 66.3% | Table 2 values assigned by the control stream `$PK` (see Assumptions) |
| BOV inflation for unobserved doses | 2.20-fold | Table 2 + footnote b; control stream `ExtraBOV` |
| Residual error | 24.8% proportional + 0.02 mg/L additive (fixed) | Table 2 + footnote f |

The supplementary control stream fixes the structure, the covariate equations
and the random-effect layout. Its `$THETA` / `$OMEGA` values are initial
estimates carried from an earlier run (for example the Antib-4 effect on MTT
starts at 0.01), so Table 2 supplies every value.

## Structural verification

These are identities of the published parameterisation, comparing the model's
own typical-value solve with itself, so they are asserted tightly.

```{r helpers}
# Daily ethambutol doses (mg base) into transit1, observations on the central
# compartment over the last 24 h interval (rxode2 returns Cc at those rows).
ss_events <- function(subj, n_days = 14, obs_step = 0.25) {
  last <- 24 * (n_days - 1)
  doses <- subj |>
    dplyr::select(id, amt) |>
    dplyr::cross_join(data.frame(time = seq(0, last, by = 24))) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "transit1")
  obs <- subj |>
    dplyr::select(id) |>
    dplyr::cross_join(data.frame(time = seq(last, last + 24, by = obs_step))) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(subj, -amt), by = "id")
}

trap <- function(time, conc) {
  sum(diff(time) * (utils::head(conc, -1) + utils::tail(conc, -1)) / 2)
}

typical <- function(cov, amt = 1100 * 0.737) {
  ev <- ss_events(data.frame(id = 1L, amt = amt, cov), obs_step = 0.02)
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev,
    returnType = "data.frame", rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12
  )
  out[out$time >= 312 & !duplicated(out$time), ]
}

ref_adult <- data.frame(
  WT = 49, HT = 160, SEXF = 0, FORM_EMB_ANTIB4 = 0, OCC = 1, SELFADMIN = 0
)
```

**Steady-state mass balance and the reference individual.** Over one
steady-state interval the eliminated amount equals the absorbed dose, so
`CL * AUCtau = F * Dose`. This pins the unit chain (mg, L, mg/L) and confirms
that the transit chain delivers the whole dose. A 49 kg, 160 cm man has a
Janmahasatian fat-free mass of 42.0 kg, the reference FFM, so his clearance is
the Table 2 value of 34.8 L/h. (A 57 kg, 162 cm woman, at the reference total
weight, has an FFM of only 37.5 kg.)

```{r gate_mass}
tv <- typical(ref_adult)
mass <- tv$cl[1] * trap(tv$time, tv$Cc) / (tv$fdepot[1] * 1100 * 0.737)
stopifnot(
  abs(mass - 1) < 1e-3,
  abs(tv$ffm[1] - 42) < 0.05,
  abs(tv$cl[1] / 34.8 - 1) < 0.002,
  identical(
    rxode2::rxode2(mod)$state,
    c("transit1", "transit2", "transit3", "transit4", "depot", "central",
      "peripheral1")
  )
)
c(ffm_kg = tv$ffm[1], cl_L_h = tv$cl[1], cl_auc_over_f_dose = mass)
```

**Formulation identities.** Antib-4 raises bioavailability by 26.0%, so the
steady-state AUC rises by exactly that factor, and lengthens the mean transit
time by 37.1%, which delays the peak.

```{r gate_formulation}
tv_antib4 <- typical(transform(ref_adult, FORM_EMB_ANTIB4 = 1))
auc_ratio <- trap(tv_antib4$time, tv_antib4$Cc) / trap(tv$time, tv$Cc)
tmax_ref <- tv$time[which.max(tv$Cc)] - 312
tmax_antib4 <- tv_antib4$time[which.max(tv_antib4$Cc)] - 312
stopifnot(
  abs(auc_ratio - 1.26) < 1e-3,
  abs(tv_antib4$mtt[1] / tv$mtt[1] - 1.371) < 1e-6,
  tmax_antib4 > tmax_ref
)
c(
  AUC_ratio_Antib4 = auc_ratio, Tmax_Rifafour_h = tmax_ref,
  Tmax_Antib4_h = tmax_antib4
)
```

## Visual predictive check of the study visits (Figure 1)

A virtual TB-HAART cohort of 200 participants: 54.1% women, weight log-normal
around the Table 1 median of 55.2 kg (IQR 50.0-62.4), heights normal by sex,
11.5% on Antib-4, and the study's weight-band doses. The day-0 dose is
occasion 1 and observed. For day 7, the six daily home doses before the visit
are an unobserved occasion (`OCC = 2`, `SELFADMIN = 1`), which produces the
pre-dose sample, and the clinic dose on day 7 is occasion 3 (observed).
Percentiles include residual error (`sim`).

```{r cohort_helpers}
salt_dose <- function(wt) {
  dplyr::case_when(wt < 38 ~ 550, wt < 55 ~ 825, wt <= 70 ~ 1100, TRUE ~ 1375)
}

# Heights (cm) are normal by sex with a 6.5 cm SD; ht_f / ht_m are the means.
draw_adults <- function(n, wt_median, wt_sdlog, p_female, ht_f, ht_m) {
  sexf <- stats::rbinom(n, 1, p_female)
  data.frame(
    WT = stats::rlnorm(n, log(wt_median), wt_sdlog),
    SEXF = sexf,
    HT = ifelse(sexf == 1, stats::rnorm(n, ht_f, 6.5), stats::rnorm(n, ht_m, 6.5))
  )
}
```

```{r vpc_sim}
n_vpc <- 200
vpc_cohort <- draw_adults(n_vpc, 55.2, log(62.4 / 50.0) / 1.349, 0.541, 155, 165) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(),
    FORM_EMB_ANTIB4 = stats::rbinom(n_vpc, 1, 0.115),
    amt = salt_dose(WT) * 0.737
  )

day0 <- vpc_cohort |>
  dplyr::select(id, amt) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "transit1", OCC = 1, SELFADMIN = 0) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    vpc_cohort |>
      dplyr::select(id) |>
      dplyr::cross_join(data.frame(time = seq(0, 12, by = 0.25))) |>
      dplyr::mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", OCC = 1,
                    SELFADMIN = 0)
  )
day7 <- vpc_cohort |>
  dplyr::select(id, amt) |>
  dplyr::cross_join(data.frame(time = seq(24, 168, by = 24))) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    evid = 1L, cmt = "transit1",
    OCC = ifelse(time < 168, 2, 3), SELFADMIN = ifelse(time < 168, 1, 0)
  ) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    vpc_cohort |>
      dplyr::select(id) |>
      dplyr::cross_join(data.frame(time = c(167.9, seq(168, 180, by = 0.25)))) |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central",
        OCC = ifelse(time < 168, 2, 3), SELFADMIN = ifelse(time < 168, 1, 0)
      )
  )
vpc_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(day0, day7) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    dplyr::select(vpc_cohort, id, WT, HT, SEXF, FORM_EMB_ANTIB4),
    by = "id"
  )

vpc_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, vpc_ev, returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(!anyNA(vpc_sim$Cc))

vpc <- vpc_sim |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    visit = ifelse(time <= 12, "Day 0", "Day 7"),
    tad = ifelse(time <= 12, time, time - 168)
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(visit, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = median(sim), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    med_ipred = median(Cc),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r fig1, fig.cap = "Simulated ethambutol concentrations on day 0 and day 7 (median and 5th-95th percentiles, with residual error); the pre-dose point of day 7 follows the unobserved home dose. Compare with Figure 1 of Ndzamba 2025."}
vpc |>
  dplyr::filter(!(visit == "Day 0" & tad < 0.5)) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.2, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue4") +
  facet_wrap(~visit) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Ethambutol (mg/L)") +
  theme_bw()
```

Figure 1 of the paper shows observed medians that peak near 2 mg/L between 2
and 4 h on both visits and fall to about 0.3 mg/L at 12 h on day 0, with day-7
pre-dose medians near 0.3 mg/L.

```{r vpc_gate}
vpc_at <- function(v, t) {
  x <- vpc$med_ipred[vpc$visit == v & abs(vpc$tad - t) < 1e-6]
  if (length(x) != 1L) stop("no unique VPC row for ", v, " at ", t, " h")
  x
}
vpc_points <- c(
  day0_2h = vpc_at("Day 0", 2), day0_12h = vpc_at("Day 0", 12),
  day7_predose = vpc_at("Day 7", -0.1), day7_2h = vpc_at("Day 7", 2)
)
stopifnot(
  # Centre of the simulated distribution against the observed medians of
  # Figure 1, read by eye (about 2, 0.3, 0.3 and 2 mg/L). A mis-scaled
  # clearance, volume or dose conversion moves these by tens of percent.
  vpc_points[["day0_2h"]] > 1.3, vpc_points[["day0_2h"]] < 3,
  vpc_points[["day0_12h"]] > 0.2, vpc_points[["day0_12h"]] < 0.5,
  vpc_points[["day7_predose"]] > 0.15, vpc_points[["day7_predose"]] < 0.6,
  vpc_points[["day7_2h"]] > 1.3, vpc_points[["day7_2h"]] < 3.5
)
vpc_points
```

## Weight-band dosing (Figure 2, Figure S5 and Table 4)

The paper simulated steady-state exposure in 1,225 virtual adults with TB
(Table S2: 56.3% male, weight 52.4 [46.2-58.7] kg, height 1.64 [1.58-1.70] m,
FFM 38.1 [34.3-42.4] kg) and compared AUC0-24 with 16-29 mg*h/L and Cmax with
2-6 mg/L. Here a pool is drawn to match Table S2 and 150 adults per weight band
are sampled from it, so the lightest band is filled as well. Every dose is
observed (`SELFADMIN = 0`) and the formulation is e-275 Rifafour.

```{r band_pool}
pool <- draw_adults(20000, 52.4, log(58.7 / 46.2) / 1.349, 0.437, 159, 168)
pool_ffm <- with(
  pool,
  ifelse(SEXF == 1, 37.99, 42.92) * (HT / 100)^2 * WT /
    (ifelse(SEXF == 1, 35.98, 30.93) * (HT / 100)^2 + WT)
)
data.frame(
  quantity = c("Weight (kg)", "Height (m)", "FFM (kg)"),
  simulated = c(
    sprintf("%.1f [%.1f-%.1f]", median(pool$WT), quantile(pool$WT, 0.25), quantile(pool$WT, 0.75)),
    sprintf("%.2f [%.2f-%.2f]", median(pool$HT / 100), quantile(pool$HT / 100, 0.25), quantile(pool$HT / 100, 0.75)),
    sprintf("%.1f [%.1f-%.1f]", median(pool_ffm), quantile(pool_ffm, 0.25), quantile(pool_ffm, 0.75))
  ),
  table_s2 = c("52.4 [46.2-58.7]", "1.64 [1.58-1.70]", "38.1 [34.3-42.4]")
) |>
  dplyr::rename("Characteristic" = quantity, "Simulated pool" = simulated,
                "Table S2" = table_s2) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Virtual simulation population, median [IQR].")
```

Weight and height match Table S2, but the pool's fat-free mass is a few kg
above the tabulated 38.1 kg. Table S2's FFM cannot be reproduced from its own
weight, height and sex medians: a 52.4 kg, 1.64 m man already has a
Janmahasatian FFM of 44.6 kg and a woman of the same size 35.9 kg, so the
source population must pair lower weights with men than an independent draw
does. The pool is left matched to the tabulated weight, height and sex, and is
not tuned to the FFM.

```{r band_sim}
arms <- data.frame(
  tablet = c(rep("275 mg (DS-TB)", 6), rep("400 mg (MDR-TB)", 4)),
  band = c("<37.9", "<37.9", "38-54.9", "38-54.9", "55-70", ">70",
           "30-45.9", "30-45.9", "46-70", ">70"),
  lo = c(25, 25, 38, 38, 55, 70, 30, 30, 46, 70),
  hi = c(38, 38, 55, 55, 70, 120, 46, 46, 70, 120),
  regimen = c("WHO", "Proposed", "WHO", "Proposed", "WHO", "WHO",
              "WHO", "Proposed", "WHO", "WHO"),
  salt_mg = c(550, 825, 825, 1100, 1100, 1375, 800, 1200, 1200, 1600)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(arm = paste(tablet, band, regimen, salt_mg))

n_band <- 150
band_cohort <- arms |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::reframe(
    arm = arm,
    row = sample(which(pool$WT >= lo & pool$WT < hi), n_band, replace = TRUE)
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(WT = pool$WT[row], HT = pool$HT[row], SEXF = pool$SEXF[row]) |>
  dplyr::left_join(arms, by = "arm") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(), amt = salt_mg * 0.737,
    FORM_EMB_ANTIB4 = 0, OCC = 1, SELFADMIN = 0
  )

band_ev <- ss_events(
  dplyr::select(band_cohort, id, amt, WT, HT, SEXF, FORM_EMB_ANTIB4, OCC,
                SELFADMIN)
)
band_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, band_ev, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 312)
stopifnot(!anyNA(band_sim$Cc))
```

## PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
conc <- band_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - 312) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(band_cohort, id, arm), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::select(id, arm, tad, Cc)
dose <- band_cohort |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, arm, tad = 0, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ tad | arm + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ tad | arm + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_res <- as.data.frame(nca$result)

band_exp <- nca_res |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, arm, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::left_join(arms, by = "arm")
```

The published medians below were read by the maintainers from the box plots of
Figure 2 (275 mg tablet) and Figure S5 (400 mg tablet); the paper does not
tabulate them. The Cmax panel of Figure S5 labels its heavier bands 46-55 and
>55 kg, unlike its AUC panel (46-70 and >70 kg); the AUC-panel bands are used.

```{r nca_compare}
published <- data.frame(
  arm = arms$arm,
  auclast = c(14.3, 21.4, 18.4, 24.6, 22.0, 24.1, 19.5, 29.2, 25.6, 28.1),
  cmax = c(1.82, 2.57, 2.21, 2.90, 2.54, 2.65, 2.35, 3.45, 3.00, 3.06)
)
stopifnot(all(published$arm %in% band_exp$arm))
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = dplyr::filter(nca_res, PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")),
  reference = published,
  by = "arm",
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", auclast = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Arm (tablet, band, regimen, mg salt)" = arm) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated vs Figure 2 / Figure S5 median steady-state AUC0-24 and Cmax.")
```

```{r fig2, fig.cap = "Simulated steady-state ethambutol AUC0-24 (top) and Cmax (bottom) by weight band for the WHO and proposed doses; shaded bands are the 16-29 mg*h/L and 2-6 mg/L reference ranges. Replicates Figure 2 (275 mg tablet) and Figure S5 (400 mg tablet) of Ndzamba 2025."}
band_long <- band_exp |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(auclast, cmax), names_to = "metric") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    metric = factor(metric, levels = c("auclast", "cmax"),
                    labels = c("AUC0-24 (mg*h/L)", "Cmax (mg/L)")),
    band = factor(
      band,
      levels = c("<37.9", "38-54.9", "30-45.9", "46-70", "55-70", ">70")
    ),
    regimen = factor(regimen, levels = c("WHO", "Proposed"))
  )
ref_ranges <- data.frame(
  metric = factor(c("AUC0-24 (mg*h/L)", "Cmax (mg/L)"),
                  levels = levels(band_long$metric)),
  lo = c(16, 2), hi = c(29, 6)
)
ggplot(band_long, aes(band, value, fill = regimen)) +
  geom_rect(data = ref_ranges, aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, alpha = 0.2, fill = "grey50") +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.4) +
  facet_grid(metric ~ tablet, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Weight band (kg)", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

Median AUC0-24 agrees with the figures to within a few percent in every arm.
Median Cmax runs up to about 15% above them, most in the heavier bands, while
AUC0-24 does not. The paper does not state the time grid from which its
simulated Cmax was read; a coarser grid than the 15-minute grid used here would
read a lower peak.

The paper's conclusions (Results, Table 4): with WHO doses, the bands below
55 kg (275 mg tablet) and below 46 kg (400 mg tablet) have lower exposure than
the heavier bands, and one extra tablet brings the 275 mg-tablet bands' median
AUC0-24 into the 16-29 mg*h/L range. For the 400 mg tablet, the proposed
1200 mg dose puts the lightest band's median at the upper edge of that range,
about 29 mg*h/L, both in Figure S5 and here, so only its lower bound is
checked.

```{r band_gate}
band_med <- band_exp |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, tablet, band, regimen) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    auc = median(auclast), cmax = median(cmax),
    sdlog_auc = sd(log(auclast)), .groups = "drop"
  )
band_med |>
  dplyr::select(-arm) |>
  dplyr::rename("Tablet" = tablet, "Band (kg)" = band, "Regimen" = regimen,
                "Median AUC0-24" = auc, "Median Cmax" = cmax,
                "SD of log AUC0-24" = sdlog_auc) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated steady-state exposure by arm.")

med_of <- function(tab, b, r, col) {
  x <- tab[[col]][tab$band == b & tab$regimen == r]
  if (length(x) != 1L) stop("no unique arm for ", b, " ", r)
  x
}
ds <- dplyr::filter(band_med, tablet == "275 mg (DS-TB)")
mdr <- dplyr::filter(band_med, tablet == "400 mg (MDR-TB)")
pct_diff <- c(
  100 * (band_med$auc[match(published$arm, band_med$arm)] / published$auclast - 1),
  100 * (band_med$cmax[match(published$arm, band_med$arm)] / published$cmax - 1)
)
pooled_sdlog <- sqrt(mean(band_med$sdlog_auc[band_med$tablet == "275 mg (DS-TB)"]^2))
stopifnot(
  # Centre of the Figure 2 / S5 distributions: a mis-transcribed clearance,
  # volume or salt conversion shifts every arm by tens of percent.
  abs(median(pct_diff)) < 10,
  max(abs(pct_diff)) < 25,
  # Lower exposure in the lightest bands on WHO doses.
  med_of(ds, "<37.9", "WHO", "auc") < med_of(ds, "55-70", "WHO", "auc"),
  med_of(mdr, "30-45.9", "WHO", "auc") < med_of(mdr, "46-70", "WHO", "auc"),
  # One extra tablet brings the median into 16-29 mg*h/L (lower bound only
  # for the 400 mg tablet, whose published median sits at about 29).
  med_of(ds, "<37.9", "Proposed", "auc") > 16,
  med_of(ds, "<37.9", "Proposed", "auc") < 29,
  med_of(ds, "38-54.9", "Proposed", "auc") > 16,
  med_of(ds, "38-54.9", "Proposed", "auc") < 29,
  med_of(mdr, "30-45.9", "Proposed", "auc") > 16,
  # Spread of AUC0-24 within an arm (see Assumptions): Figure 2 implies a
  # log-scale SD of about 0.31, this model about 0.32-0.37, and the
  # alternative assignment of the BOV values about 0.58. With 900 subjects
  # the pooled SD is known to about +/-0.01, so 0.47 separates the readings.
  pooled_sdlog < 0.47
)
c(median_pct_diff = median(pct_diff), max_abs_pct_diff = max(abs(pct_diff)),
  pooled_sdlog_auc = pooled_sdlog)
```

## Assumptions and deviations

- **Between-occasion variability on ka and F.** Table 2 prints a BOV of 27.8%
  on ka and 52.8% on F. These match the comment labels of the supplementary
  `$OMEGA` blocks ('17 BOVBIO', '24 BOVKA'), but the `$PK` code of the same
  control stream assigns ETA(17)-ETA(23) to ka and ETA(24)-ETA(30) to F, so the
  variance labelled 'BOVBIO' was estimated on ka. The model follows the code:
  52.8% on ka and 27.8% on F. The paper's simulations support this. Within
  each weight band of Figure 2, steady-state AUC0-24 spans about 13-37
  mg*h/L (5th-95th percentiles) in the 55-70 kg band, a log-scale SD of about
  0.31. This model gives 0.32-0.37, but with 52.8% on F it gives about
  0.58 (5th-95th percentiles of about 8.5-58 mg*h/L), which does not match the
  figure. Between-occasion variability on MTT (66.3%) and the 2.20-fold
  inflation are unaffected.
- **Variability scale.** Table 2 footnote e prints `CV% = omega2 x 100`; the
  control-stream initial estimate for BSV on CL, 0.0391723, reproduces the
  tabulated 19.9% as `sqrt(omega^2)` (19.8%). The percentages are therefore
  read as log-scale standard deviations, `omega^2 = (CV/100)^2`.
- **Occasion layout.** The paper defines the home dose before each clinic
  visit, with its pre-dose sample, as an occasion separate from the observed
  clinic dose (Table 2 footnote b). The model uses seven occasions: day 0
  (observed), then unobserved and observed occasions for days 7, 14 and 28,
  matching the seven `IF (OCC==k)` blocks of the control stream. The VPC above
  assigns all six home doses before day 7 to the unobserved occasion; how the
  source dataset assigned doses between visits is not stated.
- **Antib-4 effect on MTT.** Table 2 and the Abstract report a 37.1% longer
  (slower) MTT with Antib-4 and the control stream multiplies MTT by
  `1 + THETA(15)`; the Results sentence "reduced MTT by 37%" is taken as a
  typographical error. The Discussion's "27.8% higher F" is likewise read as
  the Table 2 value of 26.0%.
- **Clearance in the Abstract.** The Abstract quotes 40.3 L/h "for a typical
  individual with a FFM of 42 kg", but 40.3 L/h is the Table 3 value
  standardised to 70 kg total weight; Table 2 gives 34.8 L/h at FFM 42 kg, which
  the model uses.
- **Creatinine clearance units.** Table 1 prints mL/h, a typographical error
  for mL/min. Creatinine clearance was not retained.
- **FFM is computed inside the model** from `WT`, `HT` (cm, converted to m) and
  `SEXF` with the control stream's Janmahasatian equation; weight was recorded
  only at baseline in the study.
- **Censoring-specific error inflation** (extra additive error for imputed BLQ
  records) belongs to the estimation dataset and is not part of the simulation
  model.
- **Between-occasion etas are not mu-referenced.** The seven-occasion BOV is
  expanded into indicator-selected etas, so rxode2 warns that these etas are
  not mu-referenced. This only affects estimation speed-ups, not simulation.
- **Virtual cohorts.** Heights are normal by sex, with means chosen so the
  cohort medians match Table 1 (1.59 m) and Table S2 (1.64 m), and every simulated
  dose in the weight-band analysis is observed and given as e-275 Rifafour. The
  paper does not state the BOV or formulation settings of its simulations.
  Figure 2 medians were read from the box plots by eye, so agreement within a
  few percent is all that can be expected.
